components.css: .ds-agent-card { position: relative; background: #faf7f1; border: 1px solid #d8cfbf; border-radius: 4px; overflow: hidden; transition: border-color 160ms ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-agent-card:hover { border-color: #8d8478; box-shadow: 0 0 15px -3px rgb(122 31 31 / 0.15), 0 0 30px -5px rgb(26 23 20 / 0.08); } .ds-agent-card__cover { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 3/4; background: #ebe3d4; } .ds-agent-card__body { padding: 12px 16px 16px; } .ds-agent-card__name { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; color: #1a1714; margin: 0 0 4px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, 'PingFang SC', sans-serif; } .ds-agent-card__headline { font-size: 0.8125rem; color: #4d463f; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0 0 8px; display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, 'PingFang SC', sans-serif; } .ds-agent-card__meta { font-size: 0.6875rem; color: #8d8478; letter-spacing: 0.01em; margin: 0 0 8px; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, 'PingFang SC', sans-serif; } .ds-agent-card__rating { font-size: 0.75rem; color: #6b635a; font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, 'PingFang SC', sans-serif; } .ds-agent-card__rating span { color: #8d8478; }

narrative.overview:
This design system is built around a single conviction: the person behind the agent is the product. Not the AI powering it, not the platform hosting it — the human whose experience, judgment, and story live inside. Every surface decision follows from that conviction. The palette is warm paper and deep ink because this is a library of real lives, not a tech product. The typography reaches for editorial weight and serif authority because real experience deserves a serious frame. The components are stripped of decoration because the content is the decoration.

The system rejects its most obvious temptations. It is not a productivity tool: no neutral grids, no utility-first chrome. It is not a social network: no follower counts, no engagement metrics, no visual language borrowed from Xiaohongshu or Instagram. It is not an AI brand: no dark mode with gradient logos, no "intelligence" abstraction, no interface that makes the AI more prominent than the human it represents.

The atmosphere is a private journal made public: tactile warmth, unhurried pace, typographic clarity, restraint as a form of respect.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground (#f4efe6) with deep ink text (#1a1714): editorial, not clinical
Oxblood (#7a1f1f) as a rare, authoritative accent — not a primary brand color
Serif for hierarchy and feeling; sans for function and legibility
Flat elevation: no shadows at rest; tonal layering separates surfaces
2px border-radius maximum: sharp without being harsh

rules.name: The One Oxblood Rule
rules.body: Oxblood (#7a1f1f) is an emphasis color, not a brand color. If you are about to use it as a background, a border, or as more than one element per screen, pull back. Its rarity is what gives it authority.

rules.name: The Warm-Paper Rule
rules.body: The body background (#f4efe6) is not a neutral off-white. It is a committed brand surface. Do not lighten it toward white for 'cleanliness' — that erases the editorial warmth. If a surface needs to feel lighter, use #faf7f1.

rules.name: The Serif-for-Feeling Rule
rules.body: Serif is reserved for hierarchy and emotional weight: display headings, agent names at their most prominent, pull quotes. It does not appear in navigation, buttons, labels, or form fields.

rules.name: The Label Economy Rule
rules.body: The label style (11px uppercase tracked) is a powerful accent — used on every section it becomes AI scaffolding. One or two kicker labels per page is editorial. Six is scaffolding. Count them before shipping.

rules.name: The Paper Layers Rule
rules.body: Depth is expressed through tonal value, not elevation. A card above the page background is #faf7f1 on #f4efe6 — a half-tone step. Never add a drop shadow at rest to achieve the same effect.

dos: Do foreground the creator's name, photo, and specific background on every agent card — the human is the product.
Do use serif for headings and agent names at display scale.
Do keep oxblood to ≤10% of any given screen.
Do use tonal paper steps to establish depth, not shadows.
Do keep touch targets at minimum 44px height — the primary user is on mobile.
Do apply text-wrap: balance to h1–h3 and text-wrap: pretty to long body paragraphs.
donts: Don't make the platform's AI capability the visual subject. No gradient brain logos, no neural-net imagery.
Don't borrow the social feed visual language: no like counts, no follower counts as the primary credibility signal.
Don't use neutral productivity-tool aesthetics: no gray-on-white, no dense sidebar, no SaaS card grids.
Don't add a side-stripe border (border-left > 1px) to any card, callout, or list item.
Don't use gradient text. The .gradient-text class already redirects this to serif italic — use that.
Don't add a kicker/eyebrow to every section. One or two per page is editorial; more is AI scaffolding.
Don't add shadows to resting cards — the paper-layers system handles depth.
Don't round buttons or inputs beyond 4px.
Don't use color saturation to assert credibility — specific experience details are the credibility signal.
